title: Blue Planet III is keeping the rough edges in the age of AI
slides: Why would a nature series keep its rough edges?
Blue Planet III airs soon on BBC One
Its AI is used only to label footage, not smooth it
Viewers get wilder, less polished sequences than ever
Ask yourself: do polished nature docs still feel real?
thread_text:
1. Rough Edges Matter

Blue Planet III uses AI only to label footage, not to smooth it. That means the wild, unpolished moments stay in the final cut.

2. AI as a Labeler

Instead of cleaning up shots, the AI tags what's there. Editors then choose to keep the messy, real sequences.

3. Wilder Than Ever

Viewers will see sequences that feel raw and unpredictable. The polish is gone, replaced by authenticity.

4. Real or Polished?

Ask yourself: do polished nature docs still feel real? This series bets you prefer the rough cut.

5. Your Turn to Judge

Watch Blue Planet III on BBC One and decide: does the roughness make it more real for you? Tell us what you think.

instagram.caption:
The new Blue Planet III has a rule: the AI is only allowed to label footage, never to smooth or clean it up.

That means the messy, unpredictable shots stay in the final cut instead of being polished away.

Raw sequences are the point this time, not the accident. 🎥

If you create or publish anything, this is the bar your audience is quietly setting: keep the real moments, cut the varnish. 🧐

When did a rough, unedited version of something last feel more true to you than the polished one? 🌊
